mainTopic: Opening of מסכת נזיר: wording that makes one a נזיר, why נזיר is in סדר נשים, and the order in which a משנה explains its items
overview: The first משנה of נזיר teaches that a person becomes a נזיר even with substitute words for נזירות (כינויים) and with short, incomplete phrases (ידות). It gives examples like 'אהא,' changed forms of the word נזיר, and phrases about growing hair. It then brings a מחלוקת between רבי מאיר and חכמים about someone who says 'birds are upon me.' The גמרא first asks why נזיר sits in סדר נשים. It answers that wine leads to sin, so anyone who sees a סוטה disgraced should keep away from wine. Next it notices that the משנה opens with כינויים but explains ידות, and רבא says the משנה is missing words. The גמרא then asks why ידות are explained first. It suggests that a משנה explains the last item first, and proves this from three משניות in שבת. Two other משניות go the other way, so the גמרא concludes that the תנא uses both styles. A personal איסור is explained first, but when the איסור comes through an animal, the permitted side comes first.

steps.title: Substitute words for נזירות work like the real word
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens with a general rule: all substitute words for נזירות count like נזירות itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: All substitute words for a נזירות vow are like the vow of נזירות itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens the מסכת with a general rule. If someone uses a substitute word for נזירות, it counts just like saying the real word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person does not have to say the exact word 'נזיר' to become a נזיר. A replacement word that people use for נזירות is binding too. The rest of the משנה gives examples.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitute words or nicknames for a term
The state of being a נזיר: a vow to avoid wine, haircuts and impurity from the dead
Like נזירות itself, meaning fully binding

steps.whatToRemember: A substitute word for נזירות makes a person a נזיר just like the real word does.

phrases.english: All substitute words for נזירות
are like נזירות.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Substitute words for נזירות are binding just like the word נזירות itself.

steps.title: Saying 'I will be' or 'I will be beautiful'
steps.stepSummary: Someone who says only 'I will be' or 'I will be beautiful' becomes a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who says 'I will be' is a נזיר. Or if he says 'I will be beautiful,' he is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first examples: very short, unfinished sentences that still make a person a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'I will be' does not say what he will be, yet the משנה treats it as a vow of נזירות because that is what he means. 'I will be beautiful' also counts, so a hint toward נזירות is enough even without the word itself.

keyTerms.meaning: He is a נזיר (the vow takes effect)

steps.confusionAlert: These are not new names for נזירות. They are unfinished phrases, and the משנה reads them as a vow of נזירות even though the word itself is never said.

phrases.english: One who says 'I will be' is a נזיר,
phrases.notes: He doesn't finish the sentence, but the משנה understands him to mean 'I will be a נזיר.'

phrases.english: or 'I will be beautiful,' he is a נזיר,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first examples of phrases that work without saying the word נזיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Short, unfinished phrases like 'I will be' or 'I will be beautiful' make a person a נזיר.

steps.title: Twisted forms of the word נזיר
steps.stepSummary: Saying נזיק, נזיח, or פזיח, which are altered forms of the word נזיר, makes one a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'נזיק,' 'נזיח,' or 'פזיח,' he is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: Now the משנה gives the actual כינויים: changed versions of the word נזיר that still count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These words sound like נזיר with a letter or two changed. Since people use them to mean נזיר, they are binding, just as the opening rule said.

keyTerms.meaning: A changed form of the word נזיר

phrases.english: 'Nazik,' 'nazi'ach,' 'pazi'ach'
phrases.notes: These are not real words with their own meaning. They are just the word נזיר said a little differently.

phrases.english: he is a נזיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָזִיק נָזִיחַ פָּזִיחַ הֲרֵי זֶה נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Lists examples of the כינויים mentioned in the opening rule
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Altered forms of the word נזיר work as כינויים and make one a נזיר.

steps.title: Hair-related phrases make one a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: Phrases about being 'like this,' curling or tending hair, or growing it long make a person a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I am like this,' 'I am a hair curler,' 'I am tending my hair,' or 'It is upon me to grow long hair': he is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists more phrases, most of them about hair, that make a person a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר may not cut his hair, so long, grown-out hair is his best-known sign. Talking about growing or caring for his hair is therefore understood as accepting נזירות. 'I am like this' also counts, even though the משנה does not say what 'this' is.

keyTerms.meaning: To let the hair grow long and loose

phrases.english: 'I am hereby like this,'
'I am hereby a hair curler,' 'I am hereby tending my hair,'
'It is upon me to grow long hair'
he is a נזיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵינִי כָּזֶה הֲרֵינִי מְסַלְסֵל הֲרֵינִי מְכַלְכֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more phrases that make a person a נזיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Statements about growing or tending hair, or 'I am like this,' make one a נזיר.

steps.title: 'Birds are upon me': a dispute
steps.stepSummary: If someone says 'birds are upon me,' רבי מאיר says he is a נזיר and חכמים say he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one says 'Birds are upon me,' רבי מאיר says he is a נזיר, and חכמים say he is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends with a case where the תנאים disagree: does 'birds are upon me' make a person a נזיר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר who becomes impure from a dead body brings a bird קרבן. רבי מאיר holds that mentioning birds points to נזירות, so the vow takes effect. חכמים hold the phrase is too unclear, so he is not a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: And the חכמים, the majority view

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה moves from clear substitute words, to short phrases, to hints. With 'birds' the hint is so weak that רבי מאיר and חכמים disagree.
steps.whyThisMatters: This dispute shows the limit of the rule: how close a phrase must be to נזירות before it counts as a vow.

phrases.english: 'Birds are hereby upon me'
phrases.notes: He means he takes on an obligation to bring birds as a קרבן.

phrases.english: רבי מאיר says: he is a נזיר.
And the Sages say: he is not a נזיר.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי עָלַי צִיפּוֹרִים רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from accepted phrases to a phrase that is disputed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: 'birds are upon me' makes one a נזיר. חכמים: it does not.

steps.title: Why is נזיר in סדר נשים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking why the תנא teaches the laws of נזיר inside סדר נשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: The תנא is dealing with סדר נשים, so why does he teach נזיר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by asking about the order of the משנה. This question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סדר נשים is about marriage and laws between husband and wife. נזיר is about a personal vow, so it seems out of place here. The גמרא wants to know the connection.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (opens a point that everyone agrees on)
The order of the משנה about marriage and women

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a question about the law of נזיר itself. It is about why the מסכת was placed in this part of ש״ס.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ מִכְּדֵי תַּנָּא בְּסֵדֶר נָשִׁים קָאֵי,
phrases.english: גמרא: Now, the תנא is dealing with סדר נשים,
what is the reason he teaches נזיר?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדֵי תַּנָּא בְּסֵדֶר נָשִׁים קָאֵי מַאי טַעְמָא תָּנֵי נָזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Steps back from the משנה's content to ask why the מסכת is placed here
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the laws of נזיר are taught within סדר נשים, which deals with marriage

steps.title: Nazir follows the verse about the unfaithful wife
steps.stepSummary: The תנא puts נזיר in סדר נשים because the topic grows out of the פסוק about a wife and an 'unseemly matter.' Wine leads to sin, so whoever sees a סוטה disgraced should stay away from wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא is building on a פסוק: 'And it will be, if she does not find favor in his eyes, because he found in her an unseemly matter.' He is saying: what caused her to sin? Wine. So anyone who sees a סוטה in her disgrace should become a נזיר and keep away from wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6. נזיר belongs in סדר נשים because the תנא is building on the פסוק about divorcing a wife over an 'unseemly matter,' which hints at her sin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The link is wine. The גמרא says wine is what led the woman to sin. So a person who watches a סוטה being disgraced should learn the lesson and take on נזירות. That ties נזיר to the topics of סוטה and divorce in סדר נשים.

keyTerms.meaning: He is standing on (building on) a פסוק
An unseemly matter, here hinting at the wife's sin
A wife suspected of being unfaithful
Should separate himself, by taking on נזירות

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the order of the מסכתות in סדר נשים: נזיר is placed next to סוטה and גיטין because of this lesson about wine.

phrases.english: The tanna is standing on a verse:
"And it will be, if she does not find favor in his eyes
because he found in her an unseemly matter."
And this is what he is saying:
What caused her to sin? Wine.
And he is saying:
Anyone who sees a sotah in her disgrace
should separate himself from wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6 about why נזיר is in סדר נשים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא is building on the פסוק of ערות דבר. Wine causes sin, so seeing a סוטה should lead one to become a נזיר.
steps.whatToRemember: נזיר is in סדר נשים because of the lesson of the סוטה: wine leads to sin, so one who sees her disgrace should keep away from wine.

steps.title: The משנה opens with substitutes but explains intimations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a problem in the משנה's order. It opens by mentioning כינויים, but then gives examples of ידות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה began with כינויים (substitute words), but then it explains ידות (partial phrases).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the wording of the משנה. It notices that the opening line talks about one thing, and the examples that follow are about something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's first line says that all כינויי נזירות count as נזירות. But the first examples it gives, like 'אהא,' are ידות, not כינויים. So the examples do not match the heading, and ידות were never even mentioned in the heading.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitute words for the real term (like נזיק for נזיר)
'Handles': partial phrases that point to a vow

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix these up. כינויים are altered forms of the word נזיר (step 3). ידות are short, incomplete phrases like 'אהא' (step 2).

phrases.english: He opened with substitutes, and explains intimations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, this time about the structure of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order and wording of the opening משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The heading mentions only כינויים, yet the first examples given are ידות, which the heading never mentioned.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה is missing words
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that some words are missing from the משנה. Once you add a line saying ידות also count as נזירות, the examples of ידות make sense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said (and some say this without naming who said it): the משנה is missing words. This is what it means: all כינויי נזירות are like נזירות, and ידות נזירות are like נזירות. These are the ידות: one who says 'אהא' is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the problem by reading extra words into the משנה, so that the heading also mentions ידות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the missing line added, the heading covers both כינויים and ידות. Now the examples of ידות have a source in the heading. The order still needs explaining, since כינויים are mentioned first. Steps 10-11 deal with this.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it teaches

phrases.english: Rava said, and some say it without attribution:
It is missing words
and this is what it teaches:
All substitutes for nazirite vows are like nazirite vows,
and intimations of nazirite vows are like nazirite vows,
and these are the intimations:
One who says "I will be" is a nazirite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: חסורי מיחסרא (adding missing words to the text)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The heading mentions only כינויים, so the examples of ידות seem out of place.
steps.terutzMaskana: The heading really includes ידות too, so giving examples of ידות fits.

steps.title: Then why not explain substitutes first?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes further. Even with the missing words added, כינויים come first in the heading, so their examples should come first too.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let the משנה explain the כינויים first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רבא's fix but raises a new problem about the order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the fixed version of the heading, כינויים are mentioned before ידות. The natural order would be to explain them in that same order. Yet the משנה explains ידות first.

phrases.english: But let it explain the substitutes first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the order of the משנה even after רבא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of the explanations in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The heading lists כינויים first, so they should be explained first.

steps.title: The last item mentioned is explained first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers with a style rule of the משנה: the item mentioned last gets explained first.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא explains first the item he ended with.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the order question with a general rule about how the משנה is written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since ידות were mentioned last in the heading, they are the closest to the explanation, so they are explained first. The order is not a mistake. It follows a pattern found elsewhere in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: With the one he ended on

phrases.english: The tanna, the one he ended with —
that is the one he explains first.

steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule of how the משנה is written
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The items should be explained in the same order they are listed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה explains first the item it mentioned last, so ידות come first.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה of שבת lamps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the rule from the משנה in שבת. It asks 'with what may one light and with what may one not light,' and then explains first what one may not light with.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: with what may one light, and with what may one not light? And it explains 'one may not light' first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof that the משנה really does write in this style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In במה מדליקין, 'one may not light' is the second item mentioned, yet it is explained first. This matches the rule from step 11. So the order in our משנה follows the same pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה

steps.whatToRemember: At this point the גמרא is proving a style rule: a משנה explains the last item it mentioned first, as in במה מדליקין. Steps 15-16 will challenge this rule, and steps 17-18 will soften it and explain it.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
With what may one light and with what may one not light,
phrases.notes: This is the opening of the second פרק of מסכת שבת, about lighting the שבת lamp.

phrases.english: and it explains "one may not light" first.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדִתְנַן: בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין וּבַמָּה אֵין מַדְלִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the rule given in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the משנה explains first the item it mentioned last
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שבת, במה מדליקין

steps.title: Second proof: insulating food
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about insulating food asks 'in what may one insulate and in what may one not,' and then explains the 'may not' first.
steps.simpleTranslation: In what may one insulate a pot, and in what may one not insulate it? And the משנה explains 'one may not insulate' first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second example from מסכת שבת to support its rule that the last item mentioned gets explained first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The opening question lists 'may insulate' first and 'may not insulate' second. But the משנה goes on to explain the second one, 'may not insulate,' first. This fits the rule from step 11 exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: Insulating (wrapping) a pot of food to keep it warm

phrases.english: In what may one insulate, and in what may one not insulate?
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in שבת about wrapping a pot of food before שבת to keep it warm.

phrases.english: And it explains 'one may not insulate' first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second example of the same pattern shown in step 12.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a משנה explains the last-mentioned item first.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שבת about טמינה (insulating food).

steps.title: Third proof: what a woman may go out with
steps.stepSummary: The משנה about what a woman may wear outside on שבת asks both sides, then explains 'she may not go out' first.
steps.simpleTranslation: With what may a woman go out, and with what may she not go out? And the משנה explains 'a woman may not go out' first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third example from מסכת שבת that follows the same pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the question mentions 'may go out' first and 'may not go out' second. The משנה opens its details with 'a woman may not go out,' which is the second item. This is the third case supporting the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes out (into the public area on שבת)
A woman may not go out, the opening words of the משנה's details

phrases.english: With what may a woman go out
and with what may she not go out?
And it explains 'a woman may not go out' first.

steps.whatToRemember: Three משניות in שבת (lighting, insulating, a woman going out) all explain the last-mentioned item first.
steps.triggerLanguage: בַּמָּה אִשָּׁה יוֹצְאָה וּבַמָּה אֵינָהּ יוֹצְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third example of the same pattern.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a משנה explains the last-mentioned item first.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שבת about what a woman may go out with.

steps.title: Challenge: the animal משנה explains the first item first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges its rule with the משנה about animals, which explains 'a camel may go out' first, and that is the first item.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn: With what may an animal go out, and with what may it not go out? And the משנה explains 'a camel may go out' first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the rule it just proved. It shows a משנה that explains the first-mentioned item first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this משנה the question lists 'may go out' first. Its details also begin with what may go out ('a camel goes out with...'). So here the first item is explained first, which goes against the rule from step 11.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the woman's case. There the details began with 'may not,' but here the details begin with 'may,' so this case breaks the pattern.

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: With what may an animal go out
and with what may it not go out?
And it explains 'a camel goes out' first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule that steps 12 to 14 just supported.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 11 that a משנה explains the last-mentioned item first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A counter-example: a משנה with the same 'with what yes, with what no' opening that explains the first item first.

steps.title: Second counter-example: inheritance
steps.stepSummary: The inheritance משנה lists four groups and explains the first group, 'those who inherit and bequeath,' first.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who inherit and pass on inheritance, those who inherit but don't pass on, those who pass on but don't inherit, and those who neither inherit nor pass on. And the משנה explains 'these inherit and pass on' first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second משנה that breaks the rule, making its challenge stronger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This משנה lists four categories. It explains them starting with the first one, not the last. So now two משניות go against the rule, and the גמרא will need to explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: Bequeath, pass on an inheritance to others

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'last mentioned, first explained' now faces two counter-examples: the animal משנה and the inheritance משנה.

phrases.english: There are those who inherit and bequeath,
phrases.notes: The words 'didn't we learn' from the last step carry over here too. This is another משנה, in בבא בתרא.

phrases.english: those who inherit but do not bequeath,
those who bequeath but do not inherit,
those who neither inherit nor bequeath,
and it explains 'these inherit and bequeath' first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second counter-example to the challenge in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 11 that a משנה explains the last-mentioned item first.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another משנה lists several categories and explains the first-mentioned one first, which goes against the claimed style rule.

steps.title: The תנא teaches both ways
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops its rule. The תנא sometimes explains the first item first and sometimes the last item first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, really, the תנא teaches this way, and he also teaches that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenges from the animal משנה and the inheritance משנה by giving up its rule. There is no single fixed order; the תנא uses both styles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 12-14 seemed to prove that a תנא always explains the last-mentioned item first. Steps 15-16 showed משניות that explain the first item first. So the גמרא now says both styles are used, and neither one is a strict rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (used when the גמרא settles on its real answer)

steps.confusionAlert: The word אֶלָּא here means the גמרא is backing away from what it said before. It is not starting a new topic.

phrases.english: Rather, really,
phrases.notes: The גמרא is backing off the rule it tried to prove in steps 12-14.

phrases.english: he teaches this way, and he teaches that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לְעוֹלָם תָּנֵי הָכִי וְתָנֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 15-16 by giving up the rule proven in steps 12-14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a תנא always explains the last-mentioned item first
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retreat from the general rule: both styles exist
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A תנא always explains the last item first.
steps.terutzMaskana: A תנא sometimes starts with the first item and sometimes with the last.

steps.title: Why a person's own איסור is explained first but the animal case starts with the permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives a reason for the order. When the איסור is a person's own, the forbidden side comes first. When the איסור comes through an animal, the permitted side comes first.
steps.simpleTranslation: However, there is a reason. There, in the משניות about lighting, insulating food, and a woman going out, the איסור is the person's own, so the תנא explains that personal איסור first. With an animal, the איסור only comes through the animal, so the תנא explains what is permitted first.
steps.whatsHappening: Having said the תנא uses both styles, the גמרא now explains why he picks each one. It contrasts the three שבת משניות with the animal משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the lighting, insulating, and woman's-clothing משניות, the person himself would be doing something forbidden, so the תנא opens with the forbidden side. In the animal משנה, the איסור is only indirect, through the animal, so the תנא opens with what is permitted. The order is therefore not random. It follows what kind of איסור is involved.

keyTerms.meaning: A person's own איסור (something he himself does)

steps.whatToRemember: There is no fixed order rule. When the איסור is the person's own (lighting, insulating, a woman going out), the forbidden side is explained first. When the איסור comes through an animal, the תנא explains the permitted side first.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a משנה's order of explanation can carry meaning: it reflects how directly the איסור applies to the person.

phrases.english: However: there, where it is his own prohibition —
phrases.notes: "There" means the three שבת משניות from steps 12-14: lighting, insulating food, and what a woman wears outside.

phrases.english: he explains his own prohibition first.

phrases.aramaic: גַּבֵּי בְּהֵמָה, דְּאִיסּוּרָא אַיְּידֵי בְּהֵמָה הוּא דְּאָתֵי —
phrases.english: Regarding an animal, where the prohibition comes by way of the animal —
phrases.notes: This is the animal משנה from step 15, which starts with "a camel may go out."

phrases.english: he explains what is permitted first.
